Hi Caroline —

Thanks for the note and the snapshot — super helpful. High level answers here, then I'll attach a one-pager and loop in SEs for a short sync if useful.

1) Credits & KV/prefix cache: cached tokens are not billed while served from the prefix/KV cache. Credits are consumed only for tokens generated/served from model execution that are not satisfied by a cache hit. In practice, teams see 20–60% token savings depending on prompt variance.

2) Quantization impact: switching to int8 (or 4-bit quant) reduces GPU cost per token but does not change the credit redemption math; credits convert to equivalent token coverage at the negotiated per-unit rate. We do recommend measuring accuracy delta on your eval set — if quality drops you can qualify for a quality-protection concession during a pilot.

3) Rebate/commit paths: common pattern is a 3-month pilot with a one-time onboarding credit + a milestone-based rebate if you convert to a committed monthly band (we typically structure a rebate that offsets onboarding credit over the first 2–3 months of committed billing). For pilots that become Dedicated, we negotiate tiered commit bands with a step-down on unit price and a usage credit applied upfront.

I'm attaching a short pricing sketch and a pilot-to-commit template. Connor, can you add the recommended quant/kv cache settings we used for similar fintech pilots?

— Jasmine

Caroline —

Quick SE notes from the pilot engineering side:

- KV cache policy: for a 20M tokens/month pilot we recommend a 4-hour sliding prefix cache with a 20k token LRU per model variant; this tends to capture session-level prompts and system messages with minimal memory overhead.
- Batching: set max batching window to 25ms for interactive flows; you can increase to 75–100ms for async/worker paths to improve throughput.
- Quantization: int8 is a safe default for our 7B family; we advise running a 500-prompt eval set to measure F1/ROUGE delta — if the delta is <2%, we consider applying the standard quant tier pricing.

Operational note: cached tokens are visible in the console so you can track hit-rate (the Optimize dashboard returns a projected effective token saving).

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Procurement team —

Appreciate the clarity. High-level proposed options below; we're happy to formalize whichever path you prefer.

Option 1 (Pilot-first, refundable onboarding credit):
- 3-month pilot, 20M tokens/month cap.
- $40k onboarding credit applied to pilot consumption. If the pilot fails to meet mutually agreed SLOs (latency <150ms p50 for interactive flows, cache hit-rate >30% within first 30 days), the remaining onboarding credit is refundable (credited back as a one-time refund).
- If FastLane converts to a 12-month commit within 60 days of pilot end, a rebate equal to 50% of onboarding credit applied as bill-credit over first 3 months of committed billing.

Option 2 (Pilot with non-refundable credit + steeper commit discount):
- Same pilot length and caps.
- $30k non-refundable onboarding credit + steeper unit price on the committed bands (15–22% off list depending on commit size).

Quant locking: we typically leave quantization as a recommended configuration in the SOW (documented in an annex) and include a 30-day quality protection window after which any changes to quantization require joint sign-off for production rollouts. This keeps flexibility for your team to validate accuracy.

If helpful, I'll convert Option 1 into a term sheet and include a sample SOW clause for refundable credits and the quant annex. Thursday 9:30am PT works for a call — Connor & Aditya will join to cover ops and economics.

— Jasmine
